name: Plotinus
credit: Marble portrait head traditionally identified as Plotinus, Roman, 3rd century AD (Ostia Museum) · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Plotinus was born about AD 204 or 205, probably in Egypt, and wrote in Greek. He came to philosophy late, and for some eleven years studied at Alexandria under Ammonius Saccas.
In 244 he settled in Rome, where he taught for the rest of his life, attracting pupils and admirers, among them the philosopher Porphyry. He died in 270 on an estate in Campania.
His treatises were written down over many years and were arranged after his death by Porphyry into six Enneads, each of nine treatises. They are the foundation of Neoplatonism.
